sections.h2: Selling a Pittsford house on a short timeline
sections.html:
Pittsford owners can use a broker, sell privately or accept a cash offer. Before you pick, check the town's rules on permits, septic and village boundaries. Pittsford is a suburb about seven miles southeast of Rochester, with homes concentrated around Pittsford village.

Cash is attractive when a house needs updates that a mortgage lender would flag, when an estate has to settle, or when a move has a fixed date. With a median home value near $389,100, even a modest discount for a quick as-is sale adds up in dollars, so compare offers carefully.

The town covers 23.41 square miles in the southeast of Monroe County and had 30,617 residents in 2020, with an estimate of 30,588 for July 1, 2025. Owners live in 86.4 percent of homes, so very few are rented. The median owner-occupied value is $389,100, median gross rent is $1,534, and median household income is $145,581 across 10,528 households. Nearly every sale involves a homeowner with built-up equity and a buyer moving into the district. Investor-owned houses are a small niche.

School reputation is a main selling point. The Pittsford Central School District runs the Sutherland and Mendon high schools, the Barker Road and Calkins Road middle schools, and five elementary schools: Jefferson, Park, Thornell, Mendon Center and Allen Creek. Buyers sometimes ask for the attendance zone of a particular address, so ask the district office to confirm the school assignment before you quote it in a listing.

The Town Clerk and Tax Office collects both bills. School tax is due in full on October 1.

sections.h2: What does the assessor's calendar look like in Pittsford?
sections.html:
Pittsford assesses at full value and follows the state calendar. The valuation date is July 1 of the previous year, and the taxable status date is March 1, when all exemption forms must be on file. Informal reviews run from July 1 to March 1, any change is mailed between May 1 and May 15, and the formal review falls on the fourth Tuesday in May, which will be May 25, 2027. The Assessment Review Board has five members and meets once a year.

Exemptions the Assessor's Office handles include:

  • Basic STAR, with an income cap of $500,000, and Enhanced STAR at $110,750 for the 2026 roll.
  • Senior Citizens with Limited Income, capped at $58,400 for town and county and $37,400 for school.
  • Disability with Limited Income, with the same caps.
  • Alternative and Cold War Veteran exemptions.
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers, worth 10 percent of assessed value.

New STAR applicants register with the State and receive a credit check instead of an exemption on the school bill. The assessor can be reached at (585) 248-6230.

Pittsford requires building permits for construction, additions, alterations and demolition, pools, signs, sheds, decks, basement finishing and generators. After a permit is issued and the work meets zoning, a certificate of occupancy is issued. The Design Review and Historic Preservation Board reviews architectural plans for new structures and renovations, and the Zoning Board of Appeals hears variance requests.

Two other points matter to sellers. Sewer service reaches about 70 percent of the town, so the rest use septic systems, and a buyer will probably want a septic inspection. Fences are capped at 3 feet in front of the front setback line and 6 feet behind it. Code Enforcement can be reached at (585) 248-6265.

sections.h2: What a Pittsford seller should prepare before listing
sections.html:
Pittsford buyers tend to ask detailed questions, so having answers ready helps a sale move. Gather these items:

  • The deed and any lot survey, along with permits for pools, decks and finished basements.
  • Whether the house is on public sewer or a septic system.
  • Recent school and town and county tax bills, plus any exemption you currently hold.
  • The name of your private garbage hauler and any refuse district fees.

The Assessor's Property Sales Report and the Monroe County property portal give comparable sale prices for pricing the house.

Pittsford's tax calendar creates a few traps for a seller. School balances that go unpaid roll onto the next year's town and county bill. After May 31, unpaid town and county tax moves to the Monroe County Treasurer. If you are behind, call the Treasury at (585) 753-1200 for the exact amount before you accept an offer, because the buyer's title company will find it anyway.

Whatever is owed is normally paid from your proceeds at closing. Knowing the figure early lets you compare offers on what you will actually receive. If the sale happens between bills, ask your attorney how the current year's taxes will be split between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips and what it keeps
sections.html:
A cash buyer skips the mortgage lender's appraisal and underwriting, which is where many financed sales slow down or fall apart. A house with an old roof, a failing septic system or an unfinished project may not satisfy a lender, and cash avoids that problem.

The rest of the sale stays the same. Title still has to be searched, the deed still has to be signed and recorded, and permits, certificates of occupancy and tax balances still matter. Ask for any offer in writing, find out who pays each closing cost, and have an attorney read the contract before you sign. The more of your paperwork is ready, the shorter the path from offer to closing.

sections.h2: Is my Pittsford house in the village?
sections.html:
The village of Pittsford sits in the middle of the town along routes 96 and 31. A house inside it may carry village charges on top of town ones, so confirm the location of your parcel. The Monroe County Real Property Portal shows tax parcel records, and the Pittsford Assessor's Office can confirm specific parcels.

Delinquent taxes can lead to county foreclosure and a public auction of the parcel, and that reaches parcels in Pittsford, including the village. Anyone behind on taxes should call the County Treasury before listing.

faqs.q: How much is a typical house worth in Pittsford?
faqs.a: The median value for owner-occupied homes is $389,100. Individual houses vary with school zone, lot size and condition, so use recent comparable sales.

faqs.q: When are Pittsford school taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with full payment accepted at Town Hall through October 31 with 2 percent interest. From November 1 through 18 only the Monroe County Treasury takes payment, with 5 percent interest, and nothing is accepted after November 18.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Pittsford?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. The Assessment Review Board has five members and meets once a year.
About 70 percent of the town is on community sewer service. Properties outside those areas use private septic systems, which a buyer will likely want inspected.

faqs.q: Who can I call about a permit in Pittsford?
faqs.a: The Code Enforcement and Building Department at Town Hall, 11 South Main Street, at (585) 248-6265. It issues permits and the certificates of occupancy and compliance.
